How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City Clerk
prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the Chair’ s
discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the Community Services
Commission.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website as noted below. Public
Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the Commission
before the meeting for their consideration but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted
after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Commission but may not be received before the meeting.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

   MINUTES OF DECEMBER 1, 2025
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Vice Chair Rodriguez called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to
order at 6:36 P.M. on Monday, December 1, 2025, with Commissioners and staff in the Council
Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Vice Chair Rodriguez.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Nancy Duong, Mary Huang, Darwin Rodriguez

Commissioners Absent:  Davis Barrantes, Cheryl Cabot

Youth Ambassadors Present:  Amy Perez, Jiayi Fang

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Assistant Director Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit
comments and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services
Commission, email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT
  None.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  DECEMBER 1, 2025
 3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Duong and seconded by Commissioner Huang
  to approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for
  November 3, 2025.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 3-0-0-2 as follows:

  AYES:  DUONG, HUANG, RODRIGUEZ
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  BARRANTES, CABOT

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. INTRODUCTION OF THE NEW YOUTH AMBASSADORS
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  Staff introduced Youth Ambassadors Amy Perez and Jiayi Fang to the
  Commission and explained their role on the commission.

  The Commission requested that the Youth Ambassadors give any feedback or
  suggestions as their unique perspective as young people is very important to
  the Commission.

  B. EVENTS & PROGRAMS UPDATES
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  Assistant Director Morales-Stevens presented the Holiday Tree Lighting and Taste of
  San Gabriel Event with accolades to Pamela Scott’s efforts going in-person to many of
  San Gabriel’s local food establishments to solicit participation in Taste of San Gabriel.
  We requested 250 treats per vendor, previously we requested 500 and were unable to
  find willing vendors. With Pamela’s sales experience and the request amount change,
  we were able to get 8 vendors to participate including: Happy Donut, Paris Baguette,
  Wahab’s Mediterranean Grill, Dancing Spoons, D’ange Bakery, Love To Go, AK Fresh
  Roast, and El Pavo Bakery. The city, along with Commissioner Huang’s help, will also
  be giving out hot chocolate.

  The Holiday Tree Lighting event will also have the Trackless Train and the Photos with
  Santa. Reservations for which were already full within the first day of registration
  opening. Staff will be going through these reservations to look for duplicates and
  contacting those on the wait list as spots become available. Performances at this event

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  DECEMBER 1, 2025
   will include Dewy Woodcraft Rangers, Jefferson Middle School Choir and Orchestra,
  San Gabriel High School Marching Band, and the Polynesian Dance Class.

  The commission inquired if the Youth Ambassadors had any knowledge of student
  groups that would be willing to perform at future events to which they responded that
  their school’s dance team may be interested and that they would speak to the
  instructor and email staff. Youth Ambassadors also mentioned that there are student
  vendors at Gabrielino Night Market that may be interested in selling crafts at future
  events. The commission also inquired if Pamela would be able to go to local food
  trucks in our area to see if they would be interested in attending future city events.
  The commission requested that for Holiday Tree Lighting if we can pay close attention
  to crowd control in front of the stage that is set up next to the Holiday Tree as it can
  get hard to see if it is overcrowded. Staff relayed that sound can be adjusted, and we
  can look into stage location next year.

  Assistant Director Morales-Stevens presented the Dia De Los Muertos event on
  November 7th which was an indoor and outdoor event at the playhouse. This year we
  had a professional face painter, crafts, food from El Pavo Bakery, and performances
  from Mariachi Divas leading us outside into a drone show donated by Grizzly
  Entertainment. There were some difficulties with Mariachi Divas set up but staff
  handled it and received feedback that it was work the wait.

  The commission then requested to know more about our class cancelation policy and
  makeup classes and what is expected when instructors are to cancel a course. Staff
  explained that instructors are expected to show for the first day of class regardless of
  if they have students on their roster, because students may sign up the day of or just
  before the class starts. If an instructor wants to cancel a class, it is expected that they
  will give ample notice to staff for staff to inform participants via email and phone call
  as well as issue refunds or set up makeup classes. Staff are working on finalizing the
  procedure for instructors to be informed of these policies as they are brought onboard.
  The commission inquired about assistant coaches for when instructors are unable to
  make their class. Staff explained that most of our instructors are solo instructors, this
  allows the city to keep costs down.

  The commission was also concerned about lights at Roosevelt tennis courts and
  whether the public realizes that area is a public park or if they think it’s the elementary
  school. Staff explained that the lights are on a timer, and we have new signs in the
  works to clarify the park’s usage for the public.

  C. DISCUSSION OF WORKPLAN
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens.

  The Commission discussed the changes to the survey and agreed that the updated
  version captured all requests.

  The commission expressed interest in the city hosting a bike event and reached out to
  GoSGV who is interested in partnering with the city. They explained that GoSGV may
  have funds they can use for an event due to the city’s proximity to the 10 freeway.

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  January 5, 2026

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Ana Casillas, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Fall 2025 San Gabriel Sports and December 2025 Kids Paint Night

San Gabriel Youth Sports Program
The San Gabriel Youth Sports program, held at Jefferson Middle School, offered co-ed
Flag Football and Volleyball this Fall with a total of 60 participants. Each sport had a Varsity
and JV team with 15 players. During each sport season, the participants were taught
fundamentals of the sport, learned drills and plays, and competed in friendly games with
local cities. Both the volleyball and flag football varsity teams competed in the Southern
California Municipal Athletic Federation (SCMAF) San Gabriel Valley Tournaments at the
end of their season. Our volleyball team garnered third place, and our flag football team
took home second place.

Kid’s Paint Night

The Community Services Department offered a Polar Express themed Kid’s Paint Night
program, held on Friday, December 12 from 6:00pm-7:30pm at the Community
Recreation Center for ages 5-12 years old with a fee of $10 per person. This festive themed
event led by Recreation staff, with full roster of 23 enrollees, featured a hot chocolate bar,
graham cracker train craft, cozy storybook reading and a step-by-step canvas painting,
The program was very well received by both participants and parents. Our next Kid’s Paint
Night will be held in March.
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  January 05, 2026

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Andy Shoup, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Department Special Event Report- 2025

Holiday Tree Lighting

The 49th annual Holiday Tree Lighting was held in Plaza Park on Tuesday, December 2,
from 6 – 8:30pm, with an estimated 3,000 community members in attendance. The night
began with the Taste of San Gabriel, featuring eight local restaurants, as well as a hot
cocoa booth, Trackless Train rides, craft booths, and photobooths. The event stage hosted
performances by the Dewey Woodcraft Rangers, the Jefferson Choir and Orchestra, San
Gabriel High School Marching Band, and our own CS dance classes.

At 7pm the Mayor and City Council, with assistance from the Jefferson choir, led the
community in a countdown to light the tree, followed by the arrival of Santa Claus, who
was escorted by the San Gabriel Police and Fire Departments.

This year, several changes were made to the event to improve the overall experience. The
event layout was revised to improve the flow of the event, pedestrian traffic, and the grand
entrance of Santa. Passport Stamp cards were introduced to the Taste of San Gabriel
portion, which allowed residents to easily view the participating restaurants, and provided
the city a way to monitor and track the distribution of the samples. Additionally, the Public
Works team updated the Tree’s lights with LEDs, adding several thousand bulbs, along
with additional colored spotlights, to vastly improve the overall appearance.

Looking to the 2026 event, which will be the 50 th annual event, staff will be exploring ways
to continue the event’s success, as well as expand with more interactive opportunities,
holiday themed amenities, and of course, more lights!
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  November 3, 2025

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

SUBJECT:  Community Services Commission Workplan

SUMMARY
The Community Services Commission approved the most recent workplan at the October
7, 2024 commission meeting the Community Services Commission decided to change it
from an annual workplan to an ongoing document that can be adjusted if and when
needed to better address the needs of the department. The Commission will conduct a
comprehensive evaluation of the workplan every six months to determine if major
changes need to be made. At the July and October 2025 Commission meetings the
Commission provided edits to staff, which are included in this report.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.
 Current Workplan
The workplan sets four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore. The list below reflects amendments made at the July and
October Regular Community Services Commission Meetings.
